summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to route between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24 via eth2) with no NAT so original source addresses are preserved. Added VyOS forward-filter accept rules for both directions plus established/related state, added static routes to the peer subnet on node2/node3 (via NetworkManager static profiles on their second NIC, since NM's DHCP reconciler was wiping raw `ip addr`/`ip route` changes), and opened firewalld with rich rules on node2/node3 permitting all traffic from the peer LAN so any port is reachable directly. Verified with ping, arbitrary-port TCP (python http.server) in both directions, and tcpdump on node1's both interfaces confirming source IPs are unchanged end-to-end. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (safe reboot, quorum/independent-node concerns N/A here since this is not a clustered service), each showed a changed boot_id post-restart, and all config (VyOS interfaces/firewall, NM static route, firewalld rich rule) and connectivity were confirmed recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces and routing to discover unconfigured lan-a/lan-b NICs (eth1/eth2 on node1, enp8s0 on node2/node3)
Assigned static IPs to node1 eth1 (10.50.10.254/24) and eth2 (10.50.20.254/24) via VyOS configure/commit/save
Verified interface-to-network mapping via temporary ip addr add + ping before finalizing
Configured VyOS forward-filter default-drop with accept rules for established/related state and bidirectional traffic between the two /24 subnets; committed and saved
Confirmed net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls were already enabled on node1

Discovered NetworkManager on node2/node3 (RHEL9) was reconciling away manual ip/route commands; reconfigured via nmcli with ipv4.method manual + static address + specific route to the peer subnet (avoided ipv4.gateway to prevent ambiguous dual default routes)
Discovered firewalld on node2/node3 blocking inbound TCP from the peer LAN; added persistent rich-rules (--permanent + --reload) accepting all traffic from the peer subnet
Verified bidirectional ping, arbitrary-port TCP connectivity, and source-address preservation via tcpdump on node1 in both directions

Captured boot_id + config baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node1 then node2 then node3 sequentially (never concurrently), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified config persistence and connectivity after each restart

evidence.requirement: node1 has static addresses on eth1 (lan-a) and eth2 (lan-b)

ping tests confirmed eth1 reaches node2 and eth2 reaches node3

evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter default-drop plus accept rules for established/related and both subnet directions; ip_forward and per-iface forwarding confirmed enabled

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 can route to each other via node1, with static routes surviving the NetworkManager reconciler
evidence.summary: Diagnosed NM overwriting manual IP/route; fixed via nmcli static ipv4.addresses + ipv4.routes for the peer subnet on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port with original source address preserved
evidence.summary: Ping and arbitrary-port TCP (8888, 9999) succeeded both directions after opening firewalld rich-rules; tcpdump on node1 both interfaces shows unchanged source IPs across the router (no NAT)
